areas.name: Merdeka civic core
areas.tagline: The padang, the copper domes, the clock tower — colonial civic Kuala Lumpur.
prose: Dataran Merdeka is the room Sultan Abdul Samad was built to face: a padang, a clock tower, copper onion domes, City Hall to the north. The Federated Malay States put their civic architecture here in the 1890s, and Jabatan Warisan Negara gazetted the range as National Heritage in 2007.

Independence itself was declared a kilometre south, at Stadium Merdeka, on 31 August 1957. The stadium is now National Heritage 2009 and sits in the shadow of Merdeka 118 — 678.9 m, 118 floors. The padang and the spire are one civic argument.
Walk it in the morning, before the tour groups fill the clock-tower steps. Masjid Jamek is five minutes east, at the two-river confluence the city is named for.

areas.name: KLCC & the towers
areas.tagline: Petronas 451.9 m, KL Tower 421 m, the park they were designed to be seen across.
prose: The Petronas Twin Towers are still the pair the world knows: CTBUH 451.9 m architectural, 375 m occupied, a 58.4 m skybridge at 170 m. OpenStreetMap records them as one combined way; this twin splits that outline into two eight-pointed shafts so they read as twins.
Menara KL stands on Bukit Nanas between the colonial core and KLCC — antenna 421 m, observation pod 336.5 m. OSM has only a node; the circular shaft here is labelled interpretive.
KLCC Park is the designed foreground. The land under it is among the most expensive in the country on listing evidence; NAPIC appraisal PDFs are catalogued, not ingested.

areas.name: Petaling Street / 茨厂街
areas.tagline: Chinatown's covered market street — 茨厂街 — and the Mariamman gopuram.
prose: Jalan Petaling is the street the Chinese city kept when the colonial padang took the river confluence. In Chinese it is 茨厂街. The arcade still trades; the heritage is the fabric, not a single gazetted monument.

Sri Mahamariamman, 1873, stands at the street's western shoulder — the oldest Hindu temple in the capital, and the starting point of the Thaipusam silver chariot. It is not on the 2007/2009/2012 National Heritage lists pulled for this twin, and this page says so.
Pasar Seni, the 1937 Art Deco market, sits on the river between Chinatown and the padang. The two economies still share doorways.

areas.name: Kampung Baru
areas.tagline: A Malay reserve village inside the CBD, still low-rise against KLCC glass.
prose: Kampung Baru is a Malay Agricultural Settlement gazetted in 1899, a village the CBD grew around rather than through. Traditional timber houses and a Friday mosque sit a kilometre from the Petronas towers.

Land pressure here is the political fact: reserve status has kept plots Malay-owned and low, while the towers next door set the city's price ceiling. Listing evidence is not NAPIC appraisal; both are marked as such on the atlas.
This quarter is not a National Heritage listing. The heritage is the land tenure.

areas.name: Brickfields
areas.tagline: Little India, the railway station, and the first bricks of the colonial city.
prose: Brickfields took its name from the kilns that built colonial Kuala Lumpur. The Hubback railway station (Bangunan Ibu Stesen Keretapi, National Heritage 2007) still faces the old Majestic across Jalan Sultan Hishamuddin.
South of the tracks, Jalan Tun Sambanthan is Little India: banana-leaf restaurants, sari shops, and the temple calendar. The quarter is working, not curated.
The OSM station polygon is named KA02, not the heritage building. The pin is that centroid, recorded as a fuzzy match.

areas.name: Bukit Bintang
areas.tagline: The Golden Triangle's shopping street — 15–30% below KLCC on listing PSF, not NAPIC.
prose: Bukit Bintang is the other half of the Golden Triangle: Pavilion, the covered Bintang Walk, hotels, and a night market that still uses the street. Chinese 武吉免登.

Listing evidence for condominiums here runs roughly RM 900–2,500 psf, often quoted 15–30% below KLCC equivalents. That is media/listing summary, not NAPIC appraisal, and it is not land value under a shophouse. The atlas layer says so on every polygon.
No National Heritage listing covers the strip. The heritage is commercial fabric under price pressure.

areas.name: Chow Kit
areas.tagline: The wet market north of the Golden Triangle, still the city's cheapest inner-city food hall.
prose: Chow Kit is the wet market KLCC does not photograph. Jalan Haji Hussein and the pasar still feed the inner city at prices the Golden Triangle forgot.

The quarter sits on the Gombak's north bank, which is why flood conversation here is not theoretical. JPS InfoBanjir is linked, not scraped; OSM rivers are drawn; official zon banjir is catalogued as awaiting-ingest.
Not a National Heritage listing. The heritage is the market.

areas.name: River of Life
areas.tagline: The Klang/Gombak confluence the city is named for — Masjid Jamek at the fork.
prose: Kuala Lumpur means the muddy confluence. Sungai Klang and Sungai Gombak still meet under Masjid Jamek. The River of Life project terraced the banks; the rivers remain the city's flood machine.
Masjid Jamek is National Heritage 2009. The floodplain you see on the atlas is an interpretive 90 m corridor around OSM river centrelines — not JPS zon banjir, and labelled as such.
Walk from the padang to the mosque to see why the civic core sits where it sits.

areas.name: Thean Hou / 天后宫
areas.tagline: The hillside Mazu temple — iconic, not on the National Heritage lists pulled here.
prose: Thean Hou sits above the highway on Robson Heights, a six-tier Chinese temple dedicated to Mazu, completed in the 1980s. In Chinese, 天后宫.

It is one of the buildings visitors photograph. It is not on the 2007, 2009 or 2012 National Heritage lists this twin pulled from heritage.gov.my, and the register says so rather than inflating the gazette.
The stacked red-and-gold envelope on the atlas is interpretive, from an OSM footprint tagged building:levels=4.
